ledger.claim: The cancellation fee is conjunctive: POL-NS-01 makes it chargeable ONLY IF all four of its conditions hold, and the party asserting the charge carries each of them, so the rider wins by breaking any single limb. The limb that decides this case is (c) - a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force. For this trip that period is 180 seconds: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec is 180 and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, and under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the platform_policy figure governs because the record carries one. Limb (c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the driver's arrival tap - which is precisely the margin on which this fee lives or dies.

On the platform's own instruments the free waiting period the rider is said to have failed to attend had not been served when the driver cancelled. The wait_timer_started event in trip_record records the 180-second free waiting period beginning at 18:35:51 ('Free waiting period of 180 s started'), and the trip was terminated at 18:38:50 - 179 seconds later - with no wait_timer_expired event anywhere in the record. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable and refunds it in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force under POL-NS-01(c), and that is what the platform's own wait clock shows here.

The dwell can only be the single qualifying in-geofence run, because the traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is absent from this bundle. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no payload and has admissibility weight 0.0 - I disclose that impairment expressly - so limb (i) is unavailable and no time the driver spent outside the arrival radius can be recovered into the clock. Stripping out everything limb (i) cannot supply, the effective dwell is the single 181-second run at derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run: a margin of exactly one second over the 180-second minimum on the GPS clock, and a one-second shortfall on the platform's wait-timer clock. A fee that survives only inside a one-second margin on one clock and fails on the other should not be taken from the rider.

The chargeability of this fee is measured by the driver's arrival and dwell, not by where the rider's device happened to be: POL-NS-06 refunds the fee 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The rider track in this bundle holds 46 fixes but no qualifying fix inside the 100 m rider presence radius, and the chat_log holds no rider message, so POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record - and that is all it means. The rider's track neither establishes the fee nor defeats it, and the dispute has to be decided on the driver's own evidence.

The driver terminated this trip at the first second the minimum dwell became available - 18:38:50 against a 180-second period running from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 - and the only message in the chat_log is the driver's own 'im at the pickup point' sent 20 seconds after the arrival tap and never followed up. A cancellation timed to the second of the fee's availability is the pattern POL-NS-07's anti-farming guard exists to police; the guard does not bite on this record, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d being 0 against completed_trips_30d of 131, so nothing in POL-NS-07 requires the one-second dwell margin to be read generously - and it should not be.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:35:49, some six minutes after being assigned at 18:29:40. Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is therefore satisfied on the face of the trip record, and the rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record — nine minutes and ten seconds separate the request from the cancellation.

The GPS trace places the driver inside the arrival geofence, not merely near it. The trace yields 19 qualifying in-radius fixes and the driver's qualifying run begins at the arrival timestamp 18:35:49 and ends only at the cancellation at 18:38:50. The applicable arrival radius is 50 m for the STANDARD zone class recorded on this trip, as POL-NS-02 sets it and as the arrival thresholds block restates it.

The driver held position continuously inside the geofence for 181 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50. That meets and exceeds the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as POL-NS-01(c) directs. The trace's own shortfall figure is minus one second — a one-second surplus, not a shortfall — so the waiting-period-shortfall route under POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under cancellation reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and that timestamp falls after the required 180-second dwell had elapsed (18:35:49 plus 180 seconds is 18:38:49). Limb (d) holds on the record.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival route is not engaged. The arrival marker timestamp 18:35:49 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix from which the waiting clock runs — dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0 — so there is no early tap and no corrected clock for POL-NS-05 to compute. The platform's own wait timer started one second later at 18:35:51 and ran to the cancellation.

POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route is not engaged either. That clause governs only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m radius itself, so the driver arrived at the pickup point and the 400 m wrong-face test never opens.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. Limb (a) fails because the only message in the chat log is the driver's — 'im at the pickup point', sent 18:36:09 and read at 18:36:39 — and the rider posted nothing during the waiting window. Limb (c) affirmatively fails as well: every one of the rider's 46 recorded fixes sits between 622 m and 630 m from the pickup pin, far outside the 100 m Standard-class rider presence radius, giving zero qualifying rider fixes across the window. POL-NS-04 has no foothold.

No traffic advisory covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable and nothing can reduce the required minimum dwell. I disclose that impairment expressly under POL-GEN-02. It makes no difference to this case because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run that already satisfies the minimum on its own.

The fare ledger raises no integrity defect for the rider to exploit: the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is 4.50 SGD, which is exactly the figure platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd states for this trip, so the line reconciles with the resolution rule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the 4.50 SGD cancellation fee in force, that is 3.60 SGD. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is not '4 or more', so neither limb of that test is met and compensation is payable rather than withheld. The outcome this trip produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not a bare refusal to refund.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee shown on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02742), and it turns on whether all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. They do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:35:49. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02742) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:35:49, and it holds 19 qualifying in-radius fixes, so the arrival test of POL-NS-02 is met; the arrival marker's own timestamp coincides with that fix, so POL-NS-05 finds no false marker to correct. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell runs from that first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50, i.e. 181 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). POL-NS-01(c) expressly measures the dwell from the first qualifying GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' event or the platform wait timer, so the submission that the wait-timer start at 18:35:51 leaves a 179-second shortfall is declined: the wrong clock was used. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, at or after the moment the dwell elapsed. The rider's other routes do not open. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on, because the effective in-geofence dwell (181 s) exceeds the minimum; POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not in the 50-400 m wrong-entrance band; POL-NS-04 does not exonerate, because the only chat message is the driver's own, sent 18:36:09, and the rider's 46 fixes sit 622-630 m from the pin, outside the 100 m rider-presence radius. The traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-02742-01, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by both sides), so no outside-radius time can be recovered - which changes nothing here, because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run. The fee therefore stands, and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of SGD 4.50, which is SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the threshold of 4, so compensation is payable rather than withheld. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's charge itself is left as it stands and is not a second payment. Confidence is capped at 1.0, the weight of the GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding facts. No clause produces a referral: the arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05(ii), the RIDER_NO_SHOW code was correctly selected, and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met (the two-second difference between the wait-timer start and the GPS dwell start is well inside POL-NS-08(a), and POL-NS-01(c) resolves which clock governs). The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
